answer: Each identity is a vertex in an attestation graph, paid for the connectivity it adds. Within a rolling 40-epoch horizon the protocol counts vertex-disjoint paths from that vertex to the haven: peers already established without it. Payout follows the count, so a clone grafted onto an existing cluster adds no disjoint path and earns nothing. Profit then demands one separate, sustained neighborhood per head. Cost rises per identity and cannot be pooled, because paths sharing a single neighbor all collapse when that neighbor is removed.
